    (3) Where the circumstances in paragraphs (b)(1) and (2) of this 
section apply (i.e., because a U.S. person holds both direct and 
indirect downstream holdings in the same entity), any holdings of 
voting interest shall be aggregated for the purposes of applying the 
definition in this section, and any holdings of voting power of the 
board shall be aggregated for the purposes of applying the definition 
in this section. Voting interest shall not be aggregated with voting 
power of the board for the purposes of applying the definition in this 
section.

Sec.  851.207  Country of concern.

    The term country of concern means any of the following:
    (a) The People's Republic of China, including the Hong Kong and 
Macau Special Administrative Regions;
    (b) The Republic of Cuba;
    (c) The Islamic Republic of Iran;
    (d) The Democratic People's Republic of Korea;
    (e) The Russian Federation; and
    (f) The Bolivarian Republic of Venezuela under the regime of 
Nicol[aacute]s Maduro Moros.

Sec.  851.208  Covered foreign person.

    (a) The term covered foreign person means a foreign person that:
    (1) Is an individual that:
    (i) Is a citizen or permanent resident of a country of concern;
    (ii) Is not a U.S. citizen; and
    (iii) Is not a permanent resident of the United States;
    (2) Is an entity incorporated in, has a principal place of business 
in, or is otherwise organized under the laws of a country of concern;
    (3) Is an individual that is a member of the Central Committee of 
the Chinese Communist Party or is otherwise a member of the political 
leadership of a country of concern;
    (4) Is the government of a country of concern, including any 
political subdivision, political party, agency, or instrumentality 
thereof, or any person acting for or on behalf of the government of a 
country of concern;
    (5) Is an entity owned in the aggregate, directly or indirectly, 50 
percent or more, in terms of outstanding voting interest, voting power 
of the board, or equity interest, by a foreign person meeting the 
criteria of paragraphs (a)(1) through (4) of this section;
    (6) Is an entity directly or indirectly subject to the direction or 
control of a foreign person meeting the criteria of paragraphs (a)(1) 
through (4) of this section;
    (7) Is an entity in which one or more foreign persons meeting the 
criteria of paragraph (a)(5) or (6) of this section, individually or in 
the aggregate, directly or indirectly, holds at least 50 percent of any 
of the following interests of such entity: outstanding voting interest, 
voting power of the board, or equity interest; or
    (8) Is an entity that directly or indirectly holds a board seat on, 
a voting or equity interest (other than through securities or interests 
that would satisfy the conditions in

[[Page 67422]]

Sec.  851.501(a) if held by a U.S. person) in, or any contractual power 
to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of any 
person or persons meeting the criteria of paragraphs (a)(1) through (7) 
of this section that engage(s) in a notifiable technology or prohibited 
technology and from or through which it:
    (i) Derives more than 50 percent of its revenue individually, or as 
aggregated across such persons from each of which it derives at least 
$50,000 (or equivalent) of its revenue, on an annual basis;
    (ii) Derives more than 50 percent of its net income individually, 
or as aggregated across such persons from each of which it derives at 
least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its net income, on an annual basis;
    (iii) Incurs more than 50 percent of its capital expenditure 
individually, or as aggregated across such persons from each of which 
it incurs at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its capital expenditure, 
on an annual basis; or
    (iv) Incurs more than 50 percent of its operating expenses 
individually, or as aggregated across such persons from each of which 
it incurs at least $50,000 (or equivalent) of its operating expenses, 
on an annual basis.
    (b) As used in paragraph (a)(6) of this section, subject to the 
direction or control means that the government of a country of concern 
(including any political subdivision, political party, agency, or 
instrumentality thereof, or any person acting for or on behalf of the 
government of a country of concern), the individual described in 
paragraph (a)(1) or (3) of this section, or entity described in 
paragraph (a)(2) of this section has the power, directly or indirectly, 
to direct or cause the direction of the management or policies of such 
entity (whether through the ownership of voting securities, by 
contract, or otherwise).
    (c) For purposes of paragraph (a)(8) of this section:
    (1) Calculations shall be based on an audited financial statement 
from the most recent year. If an audited financial statement is not 
available, the most recent unaudited financial statement shall be used 
instead. If no financial statement is available, an independent 
appraisal shall be used instead. If no independent appraisal is 
available, a good-faith estimate shall be used instead.
    (2) Where an amount is not denominated in U.S. dollars, the U.S. 
dollar equivalent shall be determined based on the most recent 
published rate of exchange available on the Department of the 
Treasury's website.
    (d) References in paragraph (a)(8) of this section to revenue, net 
income, capital expenditure, or operating expenses refer to overall 
revenue, net income, capital expenditure, or operating expenses, as 
applicable, without subtracting amounts attributable to persons 
described in paragraph (a) of this section of less than $50,000 (or 
equivalent).

Sec.  851.209  Covered national security transaction.

    (a) The term covered national security transaction means a U.S. 
person's direct or indirect:
    (1) Acquisition of an equity interest or contingent equity interest 
in a covered foreign person that the U.S. person knows at the time of 
the acquisition is a covered foreign person that engages in a 
notifiable technology or a prohibited technology or that meets the 
conditions set forth under Sec.  851.208(a)(8);
    (2) Provision of a loan or a similar debt financing arrangement to 
a covered foreign person that the U.S. person knows at the time of the 
provision is a covered foreign person that engages in a notifiable 
technology or a prohibited technology or that meets the conditions set 
forth under Sec.  851.208(a)(8), where such debt financing affords or 
will afford the U.S. person an interest in profits of the covered 
foreign person, the right to appoint members of the board of directors 
(or equivalent) of the covered foreign person, or other comparable 
financial or governance rights characteristic of an equity investment 
but not typical of a loan; provided:
    (i) Neither the issuance of a secured loan or similar debt 
financing for which equity is pledged as collateral, nor the 
acquisition of such secured debt on the secondary market, is an 
acquisition of an equity interest; and
    (ii) Foreclosure on collateral where the debtholder takes 
possession of the pledged equity is an acquisition of an equity 
interest; provided that such an acquisition is not a covered national 
security transaction where the equity was pledged prior to [EFFECTIVE 
DATE OF FINAL RULE], or where the U.S. person did not know at the time 
of issuing or acquiring the debt that the pledged equity was in a 
covered foreign person that engages in a notifiable technology or 
prohibited technology;
    (3) Entrance into a joint venture, wherever located, that is formed 
with a covered foreign person, and that the U.S. person knows at the 
time of entrance into the joint venture that the joint venture will 
engage, or plans to engage, in a notifiable technology or a prohibited 
technology;
    (4) Conversion of a contingent equity interest (or interest 
equivalent to a contingent equity interest) or conversion of debt to an 
equity interest in a covered foreign person that the U.S. person knows 
at the time of the conversion is a covered foreign person that engages 
in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology or that meets the 
conditions set forth under Sec.  851.208(a)(8), where the contingent 
equity interest (or equivalent) or debt was acquired by the U.S. person 
on or after [EFFECTIVE DATE OF FINAL RULE];
    (5) Acquisition, leasing, or other development of operations, land, 
property, or other assets in a country of concern that the U.S. person 
knows at the time of such acquisition, leasing, or other development 
will result in, or that the U.S. person plans to result in:
    (i) The establishment of a covered foreign person that engages in a 
notifiable technology or prohibited technology; or
    (ii) The engagement of a covered foreign person in a prohibited 
technology or notifiable technology;
    (6) Direction of a transaction by a foreign person that the U.S. 
person knows at the time of the transaction would constitute a 
transaction described in paragraph (a)(1), (2), (3), (4), or (5) of 
this section, if engaged in by a U.S. person; provided:
    (i) The U.S. person has authority, individually or as part of a 
group, to make or substantially participate in decisions on behalf of a 
foreign person (including being an officer or director of, or otherwise 
possessing executive responsibilities with respect to, the foreign 
person) and, individually or as part of a group, exercises that 
authority to, direct, order, decide upon, or approve a transaction that 
the U.S. person knows would be a covered national security transaction 
if engaged in by a U.S. person.
    (ii) A U.S. person that recuses from the following activities will 
not be considered to have directed a covered national security 
transaction under this paragraph (a)(6):
    (A) Participating in approval and decision-making processes related 
to the transaction, including making a recommendation;
    (B) Reviewing, editing, commenting on, approving, and signing 
relevant transaction documents; and
    (C) Engaging in negotiations with the investment target (or, as 
applicable, the relevant transaction counterparty, such as a joint 
venture partner); or
    (7) Acquisition of a limited partner or equivalent interest in a 
venture capital fund, private equity fund, fund of funds, or other 
pooled investment fund (in

[[Page 67423]]

each case where the fund is not a U.S. person) that the U.S. person 
knows at the time of the acquisition likely will invest in a covered 
foreign person that is in the semiconductor technology and 
microelectronics, super intelligence systems, quantum information 
technologies, hypersonic systems, high-performance computing and 
supercomputing, or biotechnology sectors, and such fund undertakes a 
transaction that would be a covered national security transaction if 
undertaken by a U.S. person.
    (b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a) of this section, a transaction is 
not a covered national security transaction if it is an excepted 
transaction as set forth in Sec.  851.501.
    (c) The acquisition of a contingent interest described in paragraph 
(a)(1) of this section may constitute a covered national security 
transaction, and the subsequent occurrence of a conversion event 
described in paragraph (a)(4) of this section may constitute a separate 
covered national security transaction. A U.S. person should assess each 
of the acquisition and the conversion to determine the applicability of 
this part.
    (d) An indirect covered national security transaction in a 
notifiable technology or prohibited technology includes a U.S. person's 
use of an intermediary to engage in a transaction that would be a 
covered national security transaction if engaged in directly by a U.S. 
person.
    (e) For purposes of paragraph (a)(1) of this section, a U.S. person 
is not considered to have acquired an indirect equity interest or 
contingent equity interest in a covered foreign person when the U.S. 
person acquires a limited partner or equivalent interest in a venture 
capital fund, private equity fund, fund of funds, or other pooled 
investment fund and that fund then acquires an equity interest or 
contingent equity interest in a covered foreign person. (A U.S. 
person's acquisition of a limited partner or equivalent interest in a 
non-U.S. person venture capital fund, private equity fund, fund of 
funds, or other pooled investment fund may, however, be a covered 
national security transaction under paragraph (a)(7) of this section.)

Sec.  851.210  Develop.

    Except as used in Sec.  851.209(a)(5), the term develop means to:
    (a) Engage, including through or in collaboration with any 
affiliates, in any stages prior to serial production, such as design or 
substantive modification; design research; design analyses; design 
concepts; assembly and testing of prototypes; pilot production schemes; 
design data; transforming design data, blueprints, schema, or other 
plans into a product; configuration design; integration design; and 
layouts; and
    (b) Provide high-level oversight, direction, approval, conceptual 
input, or strategic planning in connection with any stage prior to 
serial production.

Sec.  851.211  Entity.

    The term entity means any branch, partnership, association, estate, 
joint venture, trust, corporation or division of a corporation, group, 
sub-group, or other organization (whether or not organized under the 
laws of any State of the United States or foreign state).

Sec.  851.212  Excepted transaction.

    The term excepted transaction means a transaction that meets the 
criteria in Sec.  851.501.

Sec.  851.213  Fabricate.

    The term fabricate means to form devices such as transistors, poly 
capacitors, non-metal resistors, and diodes on a wafer of semiconductor 
material.

Sec.  851.214  Foreign person.

    The term foreign person means:
    (a) A person that is not:
    (1) A United States citizen or alien lawfully admitted for 
permanent residence to the United States; or
    (2) An entity organized under the laws of the United States or of 
any jurisdiction within the United States, including any foreign branch 
of any such entity; except that:
    (b) For the purposes of Sec.  851.208(a)(5) through (8), the term 
foreign person means any person.

Sec.  851.215  Hypersonic system.

    The term hypersonic system means a vehicle or weapon delivery 
system capable of sustained atmospheric or very low Earth orbit flight 
at speeds of Mach 5 or greater, including hypersonic glide vehicles, 
hypersonic cruise missiles, hypersonic air-launched or aero-ballistic 
missiles, maneuvering reentry vehicles, and reusable hypersonic 
vehicles.

Sec.  851.216  Intracompany transfer of funds.

    An intracompany transfer of funds means the provision of cash or 
credit by a U.S. person parent to:
    (a) Support operations of a controlled foreign entity which 
operations are not in a notifiable technology or a prohibited 
technology; or
    (b) Maintain operations of a controlled foreign entity which 
operations are in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology that 
the controlled foreign entity was engaged in prior to [EFFECTIVE DATE 
OF FINAL RULE].

Sec.  851.217  Knowledge.

    Knowledge of a fact or circumstance (the term may be a variant, 
such as ``know'') means:
    (a) Actual knowledge that a fact or circumstance exists or is 
substantially certain to occur;
    (b) An awareness of a high probability of a fact or circumstance's 
existence or future occurrence; or
    (c) Reason to know of a fact or circumstance's existence.

    Note 1 to Sec.  851.217:  See the discussion of the knowledge 
standard in Sec.  851.104 for more information about how this term 
is applied in this part.

Sec.  851.218  Notifiable technology.

    The term notifiable technology means the:
    (a) Design of any integrated circuit that is not described in Sec.  
851.226(c);
    (b) Fabrication of any integrated circuit that is not described in 
Sec.  851.226(d);
    (c) Development or production of any integrated circuit that is not 
described in Sec.  851.226(e);
    (d) Packaging of any integrated circuit that is not described in 
Sec.  851.226(f);
    (e) Development or production of equipment not described in Sec.  
851.226(b) that is designed or intended for use in the design, 
fabrication, or packaging of any integrated circuit;
    (f) Development or production of high bandwidth, low latency 
interconnects for high-performance computing, including interconnects 
for system-on-chip, system-in-package, scale-up networks, and scale-out 
networks; or
    (g) Development or production of any of the following technologies 
when capable of use in or for a hypersonic system or its components:
    (1) Sensor, guidance, navigation, or control equipment or systems;
    (2) Software for research, modeling and simulation, analysis, or 
testing not described in Sec.  851.226(q); or
    (3) Metals, alloys, composites, ceramics, coatings, or other 
materials not described in Sec.  851.226(o).

Sec.  851.219  Notifiable transaction.

    The term notifiable transaction means a covered national security 
transaction (that is not a prohibited transaction) in which the 
relevant covered foreign person or, with respect to a covered national 
security transaction described in Sec.  851.209(a)(3), the relevant 
joint venture:
    (a) Engages in a notifiable technology; or
    (b) Meets the conditions set forth in Sec.  851.208(a)(8) because 
of its

[[Page 67424]]

relationship to one or more covered foreign persons that engage(s) in a 
notifiable technology.

Sec.  851.220  Package.

    The term package means to assemble various components, such as the 
integrated circuit die, lead frames, interconnects, and substrate 
materials to safeguard the semiconductor device and provide electrical 
connections between different parts of the die.

Sec.  851.221  Parent.

    (a) The term parent means, with respect to an entity:
    (1) A person that directly or indirectly holds more than 50 percent 
of:
    (i) The outstanding voting interest in the entity; or
    (ii) The voting power of the board of the entity;
    (2) The general partner, managing member, or equivalent of the 
entity; or
    (3) The investment adviser to any entity that is a pooled 
investment fund, with ``investment adviser'' as defined in the 
Investment Advisers Act of 1940 (15 U.S.C. 80b-2(a)(11)).
    (b) Any entity that meets the conditions of paragraph (a)(1), (2), 
or (3) of this section with respect to another entity is the parent, 
even if the parent entity is an intermediate entity and not the 
ultimate parent.

Sec.  851.222  Party.

    The term party, in the context of a covered national security 
transaction, means:
    (a) Any U.S. person relevant to the covered national security 
transaction, including the parent to an entity undertaking the 
transaction;
    (b) Any covered foreign person relevant to the covered national 
security transaction; and
    (c) Any foreign person relevant to the covered national security 
transaction, including when such foreign person is a controlled foreign 
entity.

Sec.  851.223  Person.

    The term person means any:
    (a) Individual;
    (b) Entity;
    (c) Legal successor or representative of persons meeting the 
criteria of paragraph (a) or (b) of this section; or
    (d) State of the United States, foreign state, or local government 
or agency thereof.

Sec.  851.224  Principal place of business.

    The term principal place of business means any of:
    (a) The location of an entity's headquarters;
    (b) The location where an entity conducts its main business 
activities;
    (c) The primary location where an entity's management directs, 
controls, or coordinates the entity's activities; or
    (d) In the case of an investment fund, where the fund's activities 
are primarily directed, controlled, or coordinated by or on behalf of 
the general partner, managing member, or equivalent.

    Note 1 to Sec.  851.224:  An entity may have more than one 
principal place of business, as such term is defined in this 
section.

Sec.  851.225   Produce.

    The term produce means to engage in any of the post-development 
stages of realizing the relevant technology or product, such as 
engineering, manufacture, integration, assembly, inspection, testing, 
and quality assurance.

Sec.  851.226   Prohibited technology.

    The term prohibited technology means the:
    (a) Development or production of any electronic design automation 
software for the design of integrated circuits or advanced packaging;
    (b) Development or production of any:
    (1) Front-end semiconductor fabrication equipment designed for 
performing the volume fabrication of integrated circuits, including 
equipment used in the production stages from a blank wafer or substrate 
to a completed wafer or substrate (i.e., the integrated circuits are 
processed but they are still on the wafer or substrate);
    (2) Equipment for performing volume advanced packaging; or
    (3) Commodity, material, software, or technology designed or 
intended for use in or with deep ultraviolet lithography fabrication 
equipment or extreme ultraviolet lithography fabrication equipment;
    (c) Design of any integrated circuit that meets or exceeds the 
performance parameters in Export Control Classification Number 3A090.a 
in supplement no. 1 to 15 CFR part 774, or any integrated circuit 
designed for operation at or below 4.5 Kelvin;
    (d) Fabrication of any:
    (1) Logic integrated circuit using a non-planar transistor 
architecture or with a production technology node of 16/14 nanometers 
or less, including any fully depleted silicon-on-insulator (FDSOI) 
integrated circuit;
    (2) NOT-AND (NAND) memory integrated circuit with 128 layers or 
more;
    (3) Dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) integrated circuit having:
    (i) A memory cell area of less than 0.0026 [micro]m\2\;
    (ii) A memory density greater than 0.20 gigabits per square 
millimeter; or
    (iii) More than 3000 through-silicon vias per die;
    (4) Integrated circuit using graphene transistors or carbon 
nanotubes; or
    (5) Integrated circuit designed for operation at or below 4.5 
Kelvin;
    (e) Development or production of any:
    (1) Integrated circuit manufactured from silicon carbide or a 
gallium-based compound semiconductor, III-V compound semiconductor, or 
ultrawide bandgap semiconductor;
    (2) Integrated circuit designed to, or rated radiation hardened to, 
withstand any of the following:
    (i) A total dose of 5 x 10\3\ Gy (Si), or higher;
    (ii) A dose rate upset of 5 x 10\6\ Gy (Si)/s, or higher; or
    (iii) A fluence (integrated flux) of neutrons (1 MeV equivalent) of 
5 x 10\13\ n/cm\2\ or higher on silicon, or its equivalent for other 
materials; or
    (3) Photonic integrated circuit, including development of optical 
components, co-packaged optics, or silicon-photonics integration;
    (f) Packaging of any integrated circuit using advanced packaging 
techniques;
    (g) Development or production of high-bandwidth memory with a 
memory bandwidth density greater than 2 gigabytes per second per square 
millimeter;
    (h) Development of any SI system; provided that:
    (1) Where an SI system as defined at Sec.  851.232(b) operates in 
whole or in part using an SI system as defined at Sec.  851.232(a), the 
latter of which is sourced from a third party, the relevant covered 
foreign person or joint venture develops such SI system when it 
enhances or extends the capability of such third-party system. For 
example, developing an agentic harness layer with a third-party SI 
model enhances and extends the capability of the third-party model by 
enabling autonomous execution of action loops; managing memory and 
context; or using intermediate or hidden reasoning or self-correction, 
among other functions, to solve complex tasks and format feedback prior 
to producing user-facing outputs; and
    (2) Use of an off-the-shelf third-party SI system strictly for 
internal, non-commercial purposes (including the customization, 
configuration, or fine-tuning of a third-party SI model or machine-
based system strictly for internal, non-commercial use (e.g., not for 
sale or licensing)) does not constitute development of an SI system 
solely on that basis;
    (i) Development of a quantum computer or production of any of the 
critical components required to produce

[[Page 67425]]

or operate a quantum computer (such as a dilution refrigerator or two-
stage pulse tube cryocooler), or development of software for the 
purpose of designing, simulating, testing, or controlling a quantum 
computer, or for identifying, implementing, costing, or optimizing 
algorithms and applications for a quantum computer;
    (j) Development of any algorithm or application for quantum 
information science technologies;
    (k) Development or production of any quantum sensing platform 
designed for, or that the relevant covered foreign person intends to be 
used for, any military, government intelligence, or mass-surveillance 
end use;
    (l) Development or production of any quantum network or quantum 
communication system designed for, or that the relevant covered foreign 
person intends to be used for:
    (1) Networking to scale up the capabilities of any quantum 
computer, such as for the purposes of breaking or compromising 
encryption;
    (2) Secure communications, such as quantum key distribution; or
    (3) Any other application that has any military, government 
intelligence, or mass-surveillance end use;
    (m) Development, installation, sale, or production of any 
supercomputer enabled by advanced integrated circuits that can provide 
a theoretical compute capacity of 100 or more double-precision (64-bit) 
petaflops or 200 or more single-precision (32-bit) petaflops of 
processing power within a 41,600 cubic foot or smaller envelope, or 
components designed for enabling any of such capabilities of a 
supercomputer;
    (n) Development or production of any:
    (1) Hypersonic system; or
    (2) Propulsion system capable of enabling hypersonic flight, 
including rocket-based propulsion, hypersonic airbreathing propulsion 
such as ramjets and scramjets, and combined cycle propulsion, or fuels 
or propellants for hypersonic propulsion systems;
    (o) Development or production of any of the following materials 
designed for, or that the covered foreign person intends to be used 
for, a hypersonic system:
    (1) Refractory metals or alloys;
    (2) Refractory or ultra-high temperature ceramics, or ultra-high 
temperature ceramic matrix composites;
    (3) Carbon-carbon or carbon-matrix composites; or
    (4) Stealth coatings or other materials designed to minimize 
external observation of a hypersonic system, such as spectral or 
multispectral absorption materials;
    (p) Development or operation of specialized infrastructure or a 
facility capable of testing a hypersonic system, including hypersonic 
arc jet facilities, wind tunnels, and ground test beds;
    (q) Development of:
    (1) Digital twin technology for modeling and simulation of, 
monitoring, or optimizing a hypersonic system; or
    (2) Digital thread technology that collects, manages, or represents 
the data flows related to a hypersonic system;
    (r) Development, engineering, or use of a biological system--or any 
component of a biological system--to modify, enhance, produce, or 
control any of the following compounds or materials:
    (1) An agent or toxin restricted in 7 CFR part 331, 9 CFR part 121, 
42 CFR part 73, 22 CFR part 121, or 15 CFR part 774, or novel agents or 
toxins that are capable of causing death, disease, or other biological 
malfunction in a living organism; deterioration of food, water, 
equipment, supplies, or material; or deleterious alteration of the 
environment;
    (2) An energetic precursor or energetic material, including 
propellants, explosives, and pyrotechnics;
    (3) A novel or high-performance functional material, i.e., a bio-
derived product that exhibits novel or enhanced properties, such as an 
adaptive or protective coating, bio-cement or other material for agile 
infrastructure, material capable of self-repair or self-assembly, and a 
biosensor;
    (4) A pharmaceutical compound, including, small molecules, 
polymers, vaccines, blood and blood components, allergenics, cell and 
gene therapies, and monoclonal antibodies or other recombinant 
therapeutic proteins, as well as their delivery mechanisms; or
    (5) A biofuel, i.e., fuel made or derived from a bio-based 
feedstock;
    (s) Development or production of brain computer interfaces, 
including invasive, partially invasive, non-invasive, and hybrid 
systems that enable interaction between the brain and its environment, 
as well as associated software;
    (t) Development, construction, or production of biomanufacturing 
equipment, including components and associated software or technology 
and as identified in Export Control Classification Numbers 2B352, 
2D352, or 2E001, in supplement no. 1 to 15 CFR part 774;
    (u) Development or production of the following technology or 
equipment, including components and associated software:
    (1) Biological sequencing technology, including short-read or long-
read sequencing;
    (2) Flow cytometers and cell sorters that are designed for spectral 
analysis or that contain 26 or greater detectors or channels;
    (3) Liquid chromatography mass spectrometry instruments designed 
for top-down proteomic analysis;
    (4) Computational or bioinformatics tools for research, design, 
optimization, modeling and simulation, discovery, or assessment of 
biological systems or processes; and
    (5) Hardware, robotics, or software for automated scientific 
discovery or experimentation, including laboratory automation or cloud 
lab infrastructure; or
    (v) Engagement in a notifiable technology by a covered foreign 
person, or, with respect to a covered national security transaction 
described in Sec.  851.209(a)(3), the relevant joint venture, where 
such covered foreign person or joint venture is, or any of its 
affiliates or subsidiaries are:
    (1) Included on the Bureau of Industry and Security's Entity List 
(15 CFR part 744, supplement no. 4);
    (2) Included on the Bureau of Industry and Security's Military End 
User List (15 CFR part 744, supplement no. 7);
    (3) Defined as a ``Military Intelligence End-User'' by the Bureau 
of Industry and Security in 15 CFR 744.22(f)(2);
    (4) Included on the Department of the Treasury's list of Specially 
Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons (SDN List), or is an entity in 
which one or more individuals or entities included on the SDN List, 
individually or in the aggregate, directly or indirectly, own a 50 
percent or greater interest;
    (5) Included on the Department of the Treasury's list of Non-SDN 
Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies (NS-CMIC List);
    (6) Included on the Department of War's list of Chinese military 
companies in accordance with section 1260H of the National Defense 
Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2021 including subsequent amendments;
    (7) Included on the Office of Management and Budget's list of 
biotechnology companies of concern in accordance with the BIOSECURE 
Act, section 851 of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal 
Year 2026; or
    (8) Designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the Secretary 
of State under 8 U.S.C. 1189.

Sec.  851.227  Prohibited transaction.

    The term prohibited transaction means a covered national security 
transaction in which the relevant covered foreign person or, with 
respect to a covered national security

[[Page 67426]]

transaction described in Sec.  851.209(a)(3), the relevant joint 
venture:
    (a) Engages in a prohibited technology; or
    (b) Meets the conditions set forth in Sec.  851.208(a)(8) because 
of its relationship to one or more covered foreign persons that 
engage(s) in a prohibited technology described in Sec.  851.226(a) 
through (u).

Sec.  851.228  Quantum computer.

    The term quantum computer means a computer that performs 
computations that harness the collective properties of quantum states, 
such as superposition, interference, or entanglement.

Sec.  851.229   Relevant Federal departments and agencies.

    The term relevant Federal departments and agencies means the 
Departments of State, War, Commerce, and Energy, the Office of the 
Director of National Intelligence, the Office of the United States 
Trade Representative, the Office of Science and Technology Policy, and 
any other department, agency, or office the Secretary determines 
appropriate.

Sec.  851.230   Secretary.

    Except as otherwise provided, the term Secretary means the 
Secretary of the Treasury.

Sec.  851.231  Subsidiary.

    The term subsidiary means, with respect to a person, an entity of 
which such person is a parent.

Sec.  851.232  Super intelligence (SI) system.

    The term super intelligence (SI) system means:
    (a) A machine-based system that can, for a given set of human-
defined objectives, generate content or make predictions, 
recommendations, or decisions influencing real or virtual environments, 
i.e., a system that:
    (1) Uses data inputs to perceive real or virtual environments;
    (2) Abstracts such perceptions into models through automated or 
algorithmic statistical analysis; and
    (3) Uses model inference to generate content or make a 
classification, prediction, recommendation, or decision.
    (b) Any data system, software, hardware, application, tool, or 
utility that operates in whole or in part using an SI system defined in 
paragraph (a) of this section, including an SI agent harness and an 
embodied SI or physical SI system (e.g., SI-enabled: industrial robots, 
bipedal or humanoid robots, quadruped robots, other mobile robots, 
autonomous vehicles, and unmanned systems).

Sec.  851.233  United States.

    The term United States or U.S. means the United States of America, 
the States of the United States of America, the District of Columbia, 
and any commonwealth, territory, dependency, or possession of the 
United States of America, or any subdivision of the foregoing, and 
includes the territorial sea of the United States of America. For 
purposes of this part, an entity organized under the laws of the United 
States of America, one of the States, the District of Columbia, or a 
commonwealth, territory, dependency, or possession of the United States 
is an entity organized ``in the United States.''

Sec.  851.234  U.S. person.

    The term U.S. person means:
    (a) Any United States citizen or an alien lawfully admitted for 
permanent residence to the United States;
    (b) Any entity organized under the laws of the United States or of 
any jurisdiction within the United States, including any foreign branch 
of any such entity; or
    (c) Any person in the United States.

Subpart C--Prohibited Transactions and Other Prohibited Activities

Sec.  851.301  Undertaking a prohibited transaction.

    A U.S. person may not engage in a prohibited transaction unless an 
exemption for that transaction has been granted under Sec.  851.502 or 
the transaction qualifies for the exemption under Sec.  851.503.

Sec.  851.302  Actions of a controlled foreign entity.

    (a) A U.S. person shall take all reasonable steps to prohibit and 
prevent any transaction by its controlled foreign entity that would be 
a prohibited transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person.
    (b) If a controlled foreign entity engages in a transaction that 
would be a prohibited transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person, in 
determining whether the relevant U.S. person took all reasonable steps 
to prohibit and prevent such transaction, the Department of the 
Treasury will consider, among other factors, any of the following with 
respect to a U.S. person and its controlled foreign entity:
    (1) The execution of agreements with respect to compliance with the 
regulations in this part between the subject U.S. person and its 
controlled foreign entity;
    (2) The existence and exercise of governance or shareholder rights 
by the U.S. person with respect to the controlled foreign entity, where 
applicable;
    (3) The existence and implementation of periodic training and 
internal reporting requirements by the U.S. person and its controlled 
foreign entity with respect to compliance with the regulations in this 
part;
    (4) The implementation of appropriate and documented internal 
controls, including internal policies, procedures, or guidelines that 
are periodically reviewed internally, by the U.S. person and its 
controlled foreign entity; and
    (5) Implementation of a documented testing and/or auditing process 
of internal controls, policies, procedures, or guidelines.

    Note 1 to Sec.  851.302:  Findings of violations of this section 
and decisions related to enforcement and penalties will be made 
based on a consideration of the totality of relevant facts and 
circumstances, including whether the U.S. person has taken the steps 
described in paragraph (b) of this section and whether such steps 
were reasonable in light of the relevant facts and circumstances.

Subpart D--Notifiable Transactions and Other Notifiable Activities

Sec.  851.401  Undertaking a notifiable transaction.

    A U.S. person that engages in a notifiable transaction shall file a 
notification of that transaction with the Department of the Treasury 
pursuant to Sec.  851.404.

Sec.  851.402  Notification of actions of a controlled foreign entity.

    A U.S. person shall file a notification with the Department of the 
Treasury pursuant to Sec.  851.404 with respect to any transaction 
undertaken by a controlled foreign entity of the U.S. person that the 
controlled foreign entity or the U.S. person knew at the time of the 
transaction would be a notifiable transaction if engaged in by a U.S. 
person.

Sec.  851.403  Notification of post-transaction knowledge.

    If a U.S. person or its controlled foreign entity acquires actual 
knowledge after the completion date of a transaction of a fact or 
circumstance such that the transaction would have been a notifiable 
transaction or prohibited transaction if such knowledge had been 
possessed by the relevant U.S. person at the time of the transaction, 
then the relevant U.S. person shall promptly, and in no event later 
than 30 calendar days following the acquisition of such knowledge, 
submit a notification pursuant to Sec.  851.404.

    Note 1 to Sec.  851.403:  A U.S. person's submission of a 
notification pursuant to this section shall not preclude a finding 
by the Department of the Treasury that the U.S. person or its 
controlled foreign entity had knowledge of the relevant facts and 
circumstances regarding the transaction's status as a notifiable 
transaction or prohibited transaction at the time of the 
transaction.

Sec.  851.404  Procedures for notifications.

    (a) A U.S. person that has an obligation under Sec.  851.401, Sec.  
851.402, or Sec.  851.403 shall file an electronic copy of the 
notification of the transaction with the Department of the Treasury 
including the information set out in Sec.  851.405 and a certification 
referred to in Sec.  851.203. The U.S. person shall follow the 
electronic filing instructions posted on the Department of the 
Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website. No 
communications or submissions other than those described in this 
section shall constitute the filing of a notification for purposes of 
this part.
    (b) The Department of the Treasury may contact a U.S. person that 
has filed a notification with questions or document requests (including 
questions or document requests made on behalf of other relevant Federal 
departments or agencies) related to the transaction or compliance with 
the regulations in this part. The U.S. person shall respond to any such 
questions or requests within the time frame and in the manner specified 
by the Department of the Treasury. Information and other documents 
provided by the U.S. person to the Department of the Treasury after the 
filing of the notification under this section shall be deemed part of 
the notification and shall be subject to the certification set out in 
Sec.  851.203.
    (c) A U.S. person shall file a notification under Sec.  851.401 or 
Sec.  851.402 with the Department of the Treasury no later than 30 
calendar days following the completion date of a notifiable 
transaction. A U.S. person shall file a notification required under 
Sec.  851.403 with the Department of the Treasury no later than 30 
calendar days after it acquires the knowledge referred to in Sec.  
851.403.
    (d) If a U.S. person files a notification prior to the completion 
date of the notifiable transaction, the U.S. person shall update such 
notification no later than 30 calendar days following the completion 
date of the notifiable transaction if information in the original 
filing has materially changed.
    (e) A U.S. person shall inform the Department of the Treasury in 
writing no later than 30 calendar days following the acquisition of 
previously unavailable information required under Sec.  851.405.

Subpart E--Exceptions and Exemptions

Sec.  851.501  Excepted transaction.

    A transaction that would be either a prohibited transaction or a 
notifiable transaction if engaged in by a U.S. person but for this 
section is not a prohibited transaction or a notifiable transaction, as 
applicable, if the conditions set forth in this section are met. In 
that case, the transaction is an excepted transaction. The following 
transactions are excepted transactions:
    (a)(1) An investment by a U.S. person:
    (i) In a ``security'' as defined in section 3(a)(10) of the 
Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended, at 15 U.S.C. 78c(a)(10), 
denominated in any currency, and that trades on an exchange or the 
over-the-counter market in any jurisdiction;
    (ii) In a security issued by any ``investment company'' as defined 
in section 3(a)(1) of the Investment Company Act of 1940, as amended, 
at 15 U.S.C. 80a-3(a)(1), that is registered with the U.S. Securities 
and Exchange Commission, such as an index fund, mutual fund, or 
exchange traded fund;
    (iii) In connection with a transaction described in Sec.  
851.209(a)(7), made as a limited partner or equivalent in a venture 
capital fund, private equity fund, fund of funds, or other pooled 
investment fund other than as described in paragraph (a)(1)(ii) of this 
section, where:
    (A) The limited partner or equivalent's committed capital is not 
more than the de minimis amount of $2,000,000, aggregated across any 
investment and co-investment vehicles of the fund; or
    (B) The limited partner or equivalent has secured a binding 
contractual assurance that its capital in the fund will not be used to 
engage in a transaction that would be a prohibited transaction or 
notifiable transaction, as applicable, if engaged in by a U.S. person; 
or
    (iv) In a derivative of a security described under paragraph 
(a)(1)(i), (ii), or (iii) of this section; and
    (2) Notwithstanding paragraph (a)(1) of this section, an investment 
is not an excepted transaction if it affords the U.S. person governance 
rights beyond standard minority shareholder protections with respect to 
the covered foreign person. Such standard minority shareholder 
protections include:
    (i) The power to prevent the sale or pledge of all or substantially 
all of the assets of an entity or a voluntary filing for bankruptcy or 
liquidation;
    (ii) The power to prevent an entity from entering into contracts 
with majority investors or their affiliates;
    (iii) The power to prevent an entity from guaranteeing the 
obligations of majority investors or their affiliates;
    (iv) The right to purchase an additional interest in an entity to 
prevent the dilution of an investor's pro rata interest in that entity 
in the event that the entity issues additional instruments conveying 
interests in the entity;
    (v) The power to prevent the change of existing legal rights or 
preferences of the particular class of stock held by minority 
investors, as provided in the relevant corporate documents governing 
such stock; and
    (vi) The power to prevent the amendment of the Articles of 
Incorporation, constituent agreement, or other organizational documents 
of an entity with respect to the matters described in paragraphs 
(a)(2)(i) through (v) of this section;

    (b) The acquisition by a U.S. person of equity or other interest 
owned or held by a covered foreign person in an entity or assets 
located outside of a country of concern in which the U.S. person is 
acquiring the totality of the equity or other interest in such entity

    (c) An intracompany transfer of funds (as defined in Sec.  851.216)

    (2) Prior to making a designation or determination under this

the Secretary of State, Secretary of Commerce, and, as appropriate, the 
heads of other relevant agencies, determines that such a rescission is 
appropriate. Any rescission shall be made available through public 
notice; or
    (l) Any transaction completed before the enactment of Title VIII on 
December 18, 2025 (although transactions prior to this date may be 
subject to part 850 of this chapter).

Sec.  851.502  National interest exemption.

    (a) The Secretary, in coordination with the Secretary of Commerce, 
the Secretary of State, and the heads of other relevant Federal 
departments and agencies, as appropriate, may determine that a covered 
national security transaction is in the national interest of the United 
States and therefore is exempt from applicable provisions in subpart C 
of this part (excluding Sec. Sec.  851.406, 851.603, and 851.604). Such 
a determination may be made following a request by a U.S. person on its 
own behalf or on behalf of its controlled foreign entity.
    (b) Any determination pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section 
will be based on a consideration of the totality of the relevant facts 
and circumstances and may be informed by, among other considerations, 
the transaction's effect on critical U.S. supply chain needs; domestic 
production needs in the United States for projected national defense 
requirements; U.S. public health needs; U.S. technological leadership 
globally in areas affecting U.S. national security; and impact on U.S. 
national security if the U.S. person is prohibited from undertaking the 
transaction.
    (c) The Secretary shall:
    (1) Notify the appropriate congressional committees not later than 
five business days after issuing an exemption under paragraph (a) of 
this section; and
    (2) Include in such notification an identification of the national 
interest justifying the use of the exemption, subject to appropriate 
confidentiality and classification requirements.
    (d) A U.S. person requesting a national interest exemption shall 
submit relevant information to the Department of the Treasury regarding 
the transaction and shall articulate the basis for the request, 
including the U.S. person's analysis of the transaction's potential 
impact on the national interest of the United States, and the 
certification set out in Sec.  851.203. Information and other documents 
submitted by the U.S. person to the Department of the Treasury under 
this section shall be deemed part of the national interest exemption 
request. The U.S. person shall follow the instructions posted on the 
Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program 
website. No communications or submissions other than those described in 
this section shall constitute a request for a national interest 
exemption. The Department of

the Treasury may request additional information that may include some 
or all of the information required under Sec.  851.405.
    (e) A determination that a covered national security transaction is 
exempt under this section may be subject to binding conditions.
    (f) No determination pursuant to paragraph (a) of this section will 
be valid unless provided to the subject U.S. person in writing and 
signed by an official no less senior than Deputy Assistant Secretary of

Sec.  851.503  Intelligence activities exemption.

    Transactions undertaken as part of any authorized intelligence 
activities of the United States shall not be regulated or prohibited, 
directly or indirectly, by this part.

Subpart F--Violations

Sec.  851.601   Taking actions prohibited by this part.

    The taking of any action prohibited by this part is a violation of 
this part.

Sec.  851.602  Failure to fulfill requirements.

    Failure to take any action required by this part, and within the 
time frame and in the manner specified by the regulations in this part, 
as applicable, is a violation of the regulations in this part.

Sec.  851.603  Misrepresentation, concealment, and omission of facts.

    With respect to any information submission to or communication with 
the Department of the Treasury pursuant to any provision of this part, 
the making of any materially false or misleading representation, 
statement, or certification, or falsifying, concealing or omitting any 
material fact is a violation of this part.

Sec.  851.604  Evasions; attempts; causing violations; conspiracies.

    (a) Any action that evades or avoids, has the purpose of evading or 
avoiding, causes a violation of, or attempts to violate any of the 
obligations set forth in this part is prohibited.
    (b) Any conspiracy formed to violate the obligations set forth in 
this part is prohibited.

Sec.  851.605  Burden of proof.

    In an enforcement action for a violation of this part, the burden 
of proof shall be upon the Secretary.

Subpart G--Penalties and Disclosures

Sec.  851.701  Penalties.

    (a) Section 807 of Title VIII applies to any person subject to the 
jurisdiction of the United States who violates, attempts to violate, 
conspires to violate, or causes a violation of any order, regulation, 
or notification requirement, or prohibition under Title VIII.
    (b) A civil penalty may be imposed on any person who violates, 
attempts to violate, conspires to violate, or causes a violation of any 
order, regulation, notification requirement, or prohibition issued 
under Title VIII, including any provision of this part in amounts 
equivalent to amounts provided for under section 206(b) of IEEPA. Those 
amounts are not to exceed the greater of:
    (1) $250,000, as such amount is adjusted pursuant to the Federal 
Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment Act of 1990, as amended (Pub. L. 
101-410, 28 U.S.C. 2461 note); or
    (2) An amount that is twice the amount of the transaction that is 
the basis of the violation with respect to which the penalty is 
imposed.
    (c) The civil penalties provided for in IEEPA are subject to 
adjustment pursuant to the Federal Civil Penalties Inflation Adjustment 
Act of 1990, as amended (Pub. L. 101-410, 28 U.S.C. 2461 note). Notice 
of the maximum penalty which may be assessed under this section will be 
published in the Federal Register and on the Department of the 
Treasury's Outbound Investment Security Program website on an annual 
basis.
    (d) The penalties available under this section are without 
prejudice to other penalties, civil or criminal, and forfeiture of 
property, available under other applicable law.
    (e) Pursuant to 18 U.S.C. 1001, whoever, in any matter within the 
jurisdiction of the executive, legislative, or judicial branch of the 
Government of the United States, knowingly and willfully falsifies, 
conceals or covers up by any trick, scheme, or device a material fact; 
makes any materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent statement or 
representation; or makes or uses any false writing or document knowing 
the same to contain any materially false, fictitious, or fraudulent 
statement or entry shall be fined under title 18, United States Code, 
or imprisoned not more than 5 years, or both.

Sec.  851.702  Administrative collection; referral to United States 
Department of Justice.

    The imposition of a monetary penalty under this part creates an 
immediate debt due to the U.S. Government. The Department of the 
Treasury may take action to collect the penalty assessed if not paid. 
In addition or instead, the matter may be referred to the Department of 
Justice for appropriate action to recover the penalty.

Sec.  851.703  Divestment.

    (a) The Secretary may compel the divestment of a covered national 
security transaction in a prohibited technology.
    (b) The Secretary may refer any action taken under paragraph (a) of 
this section to the Attorney General to seek appropriate relief to 
enforce such action, including divestment or other relief.

Sec.  851.704  Voluntary self-disclosure.

    (a) Any person that has engaged in conduct that may constitute a 
violation of this part may submit a voluntary self-disclosure of that 
conduct to the Department of the Treasury.
    (b) In determining the appropriate response to any violation, the 
Department of the Treasury will consider the submission and the 
timeliness of any voluntary self-disclosure.
    (c) In assessing the timeliness of a voluntary self-disclosure, the 
Department of the Treasury will consider whether it has learned of the 
conduct prior to the voluntary self-disclosure. The Department of the 
Treasury may consider disclosure of a violation to another government 
agency other than the Department of the Treasury as a voluntary self-
disclosure based on a case-by-case assessment.
    (d) Notwithstanding paragraphs (a) through (c) of this section, 
identification to the Department of the Treasury of conduct that may 
constitute a violation of this part may not be assessed to be a 
voluntary self-disclosure in one or more of the following 
circumstances:
    (1) A different party has provided a prior disclosure to the 
Department of the Treasury of the conduct or similar conduct related to 
the same pattern or practice, regardless of whether the disclosing 
person knew of the different party's prior disclosure;
    (2) The disclosure includes materially false or misleading 
information;
    (3) The disclosure, when considered along with supplemental 
information timely provided by the disclosing person, is materially 
incomplete;
    (4) The disclosure is not self-initiated, including when the 
disclosure results from a suggestion or order of a Federal or state 
agency or official;
    (5) The disclosure is a response to an administrative subpoena or 
other inquiry from the Department of the Treasury or another government 
agency;

[[Page 67431]]

    (6) The disclosure is made about the conduct of an entity by an 
individual in such entity without the authorization of such entity's 
senior management; or
    (7) The filing is made pursuant to a required notification under 
this part, including Sec.  851.403 or Sec.  851.406.
    (e) A voluntary self-disclosure to the Department of the Treasury 
must take the form of a written letter submitted through the electronic 
Outbound Notification System and addressed to the Assistant Secretary 
for Investment Security describing the conduct that may constitute a 
violation and each of the persons involved. Specifically, the letter 
must include, or be followed within a reasonable period by supplemental 
information that contains sufficient detail to afford a complete 
understanding of the conduct that may constitute the violation, 
including;
    (1) Whether the relevant covered national security transaction (or 
transactions) was in a notifiable technology or prohibited technology, 
with reference to the relevant paragraph of Sec.  851.218 or Sec.  
851.226;
    (2) The date or dates on which the conduct occurred;
    (3) The parties to the transaction(s);
    (4) Whether any of the parties have established programs or 
protocols aimed at compliance with the regulations in this part;
    (5) A description of any pre-transaction diligence undertaken by 
the U.S. person, including, as applicable, any steps described in Sec.  
851.104(c);
    (6) A statement of the reason why the transaction was undertaken in 
light of the regulations in this part; and
    (7) A proposal for mitigation of any harms associated with the 
violation, which may include divestment or a voluntary disgorgement of 
profits.
    (f) A person making a voluntary self-disclosure must respond to any 
follow-up inquiries by the Department of the Treasury within the time 
frame and in the manner specified by the Department of the Treasury.

Subpart H--Provision and Handling of Information

Sec.  851.801  Confidentiality.

    (a) Except to the extent required by law or otherwise provided in 
paragraph (b) of this section, any information or documentary materials 
not otherwise publicly available that are submitted to or filed with 
the Department of the Treasury under this part, including in connection 
with a compliance inquiry or action under subpart F of this part, shall 
be exempt from disclosure under 5 U.S.C. 552(b)(3), and no such 
material may be made public.
    (b) Notwithstanding paragraph (a) of this section, except to the 
extent prohibited by law, the Department of the Treasury may disclose 
information or documentary materials that are not otherwise publicly 
available, subject to appropriate confidentiality and classification 
requirements, when such information is or documentary materials are:
    (1) Relevant to any judicial or administrative action or 
proceeding;
    (2) Provided to Congress or to any duly authorized committee or 
subcommittee of Congress;
    (3) Important to the national security analysis or actions of the 
Secretary to any domestic governmental entity, or to any foreign 
governmental entity of a U.S. ally or partner, only to the extent 
necessary for national security purposes;
    (4) The identity of a covered foreign person in any public database 
established under section 805 of Title VIII;
    (5) Information that the submitting or filing parties have 
consented to be disclosed to non-parties; or
    (6) Gathered by the Secretary or the Secretary's designee where the 
disclosure is determined by the Secretary or the Secretary's designee 
to be in the national interest, which may include publication of 
anonymized data.

Sec.  851.802  Language of information.

    All materials or information submitted or filed with the Department 
of the Treasury under this part shall be submitted in English. If 
supplementary or additional materials were originally written in a 
foreign language, they shall be submitted in their original language. 
Where English versions of those documents exist, they shall also be 
submitted.

Subpart I--Non-Binding Feedback

Sec.  851.901   Eligibility to request feedback.

    (a) This subpart establishes procedures by which an eligible person 
may request non-binding feedback from the Department of the Treasury as 
to whether a transaction would constitute a prohibited transaction 
under this part.
    (b) Only a person with a direct financial interest in the subject 
transaction may submit a request under this subpart.
    (c) The transaction that is the subject of the request must be an 
actual--not hypothetical--transaction and involve only prospective 
conduct (i.e., conduct that has not yet occurred). An executed contract 
is not required, but the material terms of the prospective transaction 
must be identified in a binding written agreement or other binding 
document to demonstrate that the transaction is not hypothetical.

    Note 1 to Sec.  851.901:  Because feedback may only be requested 
for prospective conduct, submission of a voluntary self-disclosure 
under Sec.  851.704 does not constitute a request under this 
subpart.

Sec.  851.902  Submission requirements.

    (a) A request for non-binding feedback must be submitted in 
writing.
    (b) A request must be submitted in accordance with the instructions 
found on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment Security 
Program website or as otherwise specified by the Department of the 
Treasury.
    (c) A request must address a single transaction.
    (d) A request must include all relevant and material information 
bearing on whether the subject transaction would constitute a 
prohibited transaction, including:
    (1) Identification of the requester and any other persons joining 
in the request, including name, address, place of incorporation or 
organization (if applicable), principal place of business, citizenship, 
and points of contact;
    (2) Identification of each party to the transaction (including 
relevant intermediaries, financing sources, and controlled foreign 
entities), and each covered foreign person, if known;
    (3) A detailed description of the contemplated structure of the 
transaction, including the form of investment, governance and 
information rights, timing, and completion date;
    (4) A detailed description of the products, services, technologies, 
or activities implicated by the transaction and the basis for the 
requester's view as to whether such products, services, technologies, 
or activities may constitute prohibited technology;
    (5) All operative documents and material term sheets, draft 
agreements, side letters, and other written materials reflecting the 
contemplated transaction, as available at the time of submission;
    (6) Any other information that the requester believes is relevant 
to the application of this part to the transaction, including any prior 
submissions to the Department of the Treasury under this part or part 
850 of this chapter concerning the same or closely related transaction, 
or any other information that may be material to the subject 
transaction; and
    (7) A statement as to whether the requester seeks:
    (i) Anonymized guidance to the public; or
    (ii) Confidential non-binding feedback provided to the requester.

[[Page 67432]]

    (e) A request must be signed by an authorized representative of the 
requester or by counsel expressly authorized in writing to sign on the 
requester's behalf and the signer must certify
    (1) That the request contains a true, correct, and complete 
disclosure of all material facts and circumstances known to the 
requester at the time of submission; and
    (2) That the requester will promptly supplement the request if the 
requester learns of material changes to facts stated in the request or 
omissions therefrom.
    (f) A requester may identify in its submission any information that 
it considers proprietary or identifying to assist in the event 
anonymized guidance is issued to the public.

Sec.  851.903  Additional information; completeness.

    (a) If a request does not contain all information the Department of 
the Treasury deems necessary to review the matter, the Department of 
the Treasury may request additional information or documents, or a 
meeting with the requester and any other relevant parties to the 
transaction.
    (b) Failure to provide requested information within the time frame 
specified by the Department of the Treasury may result in the closing 
of the request without providing feedback.
    (c) A request will not be deemed complete until the Department of 
the Treasury receives all additional information it has requested.

    Note 1 to Sec.  851.903:  The Department of the Treasury may 
request additional information from other relevant parties to 
conduct its analysis.

Sec.  851.904   Issuance of non-binding feedback.

    (a) Receipt of a complete request for non-binding feedback by an 
eligible person under this subpart does not obligate the Department of 
the Treasury to issue such feedback.
    (b) The Department of the Treasury may, in its sole discretion, 
respond to a complete request by providing anonymized public guidance, 
issuing confidential, written non-binding feedback stating the 
Department of the Treasury's view as to whether the transaction, as 
described, would constitute a covered national security transaction in 
a prohibited technology, or declining to provide feedback. When 
providing feedback, the Department of the Treasury may, in its sole 
discretion, respond to some, but not all, of the questions or 
information provided by the requestor (e.g., non-binding feedback 
limited to whether the foreign person is a covered foreign person).
    (c) No oral clearance, release, or other statement purporting to 
provide non-binding feedback under this subpart may be given.
    (d) Non-binding feedback does not express the Department of the 
Treasury's views on any legal or factual issues that may arise under 
other statutes or regulations, or before any other department or 
agency.
    (e) Non-binding feedback may be invalidated, modified, or revoked 
by the Department of the Treasury at any time, including if it was 
based on inaccurate, incomplete, or outdated information.

Sec.  851.905  Effect of non-binding feedback.

    (a) Any non-binding feedback issued under this subpart is not 
binding on the Department of the Treasury, any other Federal or local 
department or agency, or any court; does not constitute an 
authorization, license, exemption, or waiver; and does not preclude the 
Department of the Treasury from taking any action authorized by law 
with respect to the transaction, the requester, or any other person.
    (b) In determining an appropriate response to a potential violation 
under this part, the Department of the Treasury may consider, among 
other factors, whether the requester sought and reasonably acted 
consistent with non-binding feedback, provided that the requester made 
a true, correct, and complete disclosure of all material facts and 
circumstances known to the requester at the time of submission.

Sec.  851.906  Anonymized public guidance.

    Anonymized public guidance issued pursuant to this subpart may take 
the form of answers to frequently asked questions, standalone 
regulatory guidance, or anonymized versions of the feedback provided to 
a requestor.

Sec.  851.907   Limitations; frivolous feedback requests.

    (a) In establishing and administering processes under this subpart, 
the Department of the Treasury may reject or otherwise limit any 
request identified as frivolous. The Department of the Treasury may 
identify a request as frivolous in its sole discretion and based on a 
totality of the circumstances, including whether the request:
    (1) Lacks sufficient detail or supporting materials to permit 
meaningful review;
    (2) Duplicates, without material change, a prior request by the 
same requester;
    (3) Seeks general advisory views or policy guidance not specific to 
the transaction described;
    (4) Is submitted in bad faith, for purposes of delay, harassment, 
or to burden the Department of the Treasury; or
    (5) Otherwise fails to further the administration or enforcement of 
this part.
    (b) The Department of the Treasury, in its sole discretion, may 
place limitations on a requester that submits a frivolous request. Such 
limitations may include declining to accept the request, closing the 
request, requiring consolidation of multiple requests, limiting the 
number of requests submitted by a requester within a specified period, 
or requiring pre-submission consultation, as specified by the 
Department of the Treasury through public notice or instructions 
published on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment 
Security Program website.

Sec.  851.908  Signature requirement.

    Confidential non-binding feedback must be signed by the Assistant 
Secretary of the Treasury for Investment Security, a Deputy Assistant 
Secretary for Investment Security, or another official acting pursuant 
to Sec.  851.1101 or other applicable delegation.

Subpart J--Information on Covered Foreign Persons

Sec.  851.1001  Confidential submission of information on covered 
foreign persons.

    (a) Any person may submit information, including supporting 
documents, to the Department of the Treasury regarding whether a 
foreign person is a covered foreign person engaged in a prohibited 
technology or in a notifiable technology. Submission instructions are 
available on the Department of the Treasury's Outbound Investment 
Security Program website.
    (b) A person submitting information must include their:
    (1) Full legal name (last, first, middle name);
    (2) Occupation or line of work, including name of employer (if 
any); and
    (3) Contact information.
    (c) The submission must include the following information, as 
applicable, and to the best of the submitter's ability, about the 
foreign person that is the subject of the confidential submission:
    (1) Name, including any known aliases;
    (2) Principal place(s) of business;
    (3) Place of incorporation or legal organization;
    (4) Company address(es);
    (5) Company website;
    (6) Any information regarding the foreign person's nationality (if 
an

[[Page 67433]]

individual) or ownership (if an entity), including the foreign person's 
ultimate owner, and the full legal names and titles of each officer, 
director, and other member of management of the foreign person;
    (7) The notifiable technology or prohibited technology in which the 
foreign person is engaged by reference to the relevant paragraph under 
Sec.  851.218 or Sec.  851.226, as appropriate; and
    (8) Any other information that the submitter believes would assist 
the Department of the Treasury to analyze and understand the 
information submitted.
    (d) The submission must also include an explanation regarding how 
the submitter determined or discovered that the foreign person is 
engaged in a prohibited technology or a notifiable technology. If the 
explanation refers to specific documents or other materials, the 
submitter should, if possible, provide such documents or materials as 
part of the submission.
    (e) The Department of the Treasury may contact the submitter with 
follow-up inquiries regarding the submission.
    (f) The Department of the Treasury, in its sole discretion, may 
place limitations on a person that makes frivolous or bad faith 
submissions of information. Such limitations may include prohibiting 
the person from making additional submissions or limiting the number of 
submissions that may be made within a specified period.
